### workspace daemon --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace daemon status [WORKSPACE] [--name NAME] [--json]
       workspace daemon restart [WORKSPACE] [--name NAME] [--wc-socket PATH] [--json]
       workspace daemon restart --all [--json]
       workspace daemon log [WORKSPACE] [--name NAME] [--lines N] [--json]
       workspace daemon list [--json]

Inspect or control a workspace's agent daemon (see `workspace agentd`).
  status   Say whether a workspace's agent daemon answers
  restart  Stop a workspace's agent daemon and start a new one in the background
  log      Show the last lines of a workspace's agent daemon log
  list     List every running agent daemon
Run `workspace daemon VERB --help` for a verb's options.

        --name NAME                  Workspace name (defaults to WORKSPACE or the project detected from the current directory)
        --lines N                    log: how many trailing lines (default 40)
        --wc-socket PATH             restart: work-coordinator socket for the new daemon (default: the old daemon's)
        --all                        restart: restart every running daemon instead of one workspace
        --json                       Print one JSON document (see docs/README.daemon.md)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace daemon list    # every running daemon
  workspace daemon status my-app    # is its daemon answering
  workspace daemon log my-app --lines 100    # the last 100 lines of its log
  workspace daemon restart my-app --json    # one JSON action document
  workspace daemon restart --all    # SIGTERM each running daemon and start it again
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace daemon status --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace daemon status [WORKSPACE] [--name NAME] [--json]

Say whether a workspace's agent daemon answers.

The agent daemon (`workspace agentd`) watches a workspace's panes. This shows whether it answers on
its socket, its pid, and its socket and log paths.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Same as the WORKSPACE argument (default: the project detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace daemon status    # is the daemon of the project in the current directory answering
  workspace daemon status my-app    # the same for a named workspace; not running is an answer (exit 0)
  workspace daemon status --name my-app --json    # one JSON document with running, pid, socket and log
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace daemon restart --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace daemon restart [WORKSPACE] [--name NAME] [--wc-socket PATH] [--json]
       workspace daemon restart --all [--json]

Stop a workspace's agent daemon and start a new one in the background.

The agent daemon (`workspace agentd`) watches a workspace's panes. Restart stops the daemon holding
the socket (SIGTERM, even a hung one) and starts a new one in the background; a daemon run in a
terminal is replaced by a detached one. With none running, it just starts one.

--all restarts every running daemon, one after another, so each runs the code that is installed
now; one that fails does not stop the rest, and the exit status is non-zero if any failed. It takes
no workspace, --name or --wc-socket.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Same as the WORKSPACE argument (default: the project detected from the current directory)
    --wc-socket PATH             Work-coordinator socket for the new daemon (default: the old daemon's)
    --all                        Restart every running daemon instead of one workspace
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace daemon restart    # SIGTERM this project's daemon, then start a new one in the background (just start one if none runs)
  workspace daemon restart my-app --wc-socket /tmp/wc-dev.sock    # the new daemon uses another coordinator socket
  workspace daemon restart --all    # SIGTERM each running daemon and start it again, so each runs the installed version
  workspace daemon restart my-app --json    # one JSON action document; exits 1 if the restart failed
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace daemon log --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace daemon log [WORKSPACE] [--name NAME] [--lines N] [--json]

Show the last lines of a workspace's agent daemon log.

Only a background daemon writes this log; a daemon run in a terminal logs to that terminal instead.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Same as the WORKSPACE argument (default: the project detected from the current directory)
    --lines N                    How many trailing lines, 1 to 10000 (default: 40)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace daemon log    # the last 40 lines for the project in the current directory
  workspace daemon log my-app --lines 100    # more of a named workspace's log
  workspace daemon log --name my-app --json    # the lines, the log's path and whether the file exists, as JSON
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace daemon list --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace daemon list [--json]

List every running agent daemon.

Shows each daemon's workspace, pid, start time and socket. It takes no workspace.

Options:
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace daemon list    # every running daemon; prints a message and exits 0 when none run
  workspace daemon list --json    # one JSON document with a row per daemon
  workspace daemon list --json | jq -r '.daemons[].workspace'    # the workspaces that have a daemon running
--- stderr
--- end
